region: Hector · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
title: 2023 Chateau LaFayette Reneau Finger Lakes Cabernet Sauvignon
about: In 1985 Dick and Betty Reno, who had fallen for the Finger Lakes on holiday, bought an old brick farmhouse and a 140-acre farm on the south-eastern slopes of Seneca Lake, near Hector. It had been the Loomis family’s fruit farm, shipping grapes and fruit down the Erie Canal to New York City, and its fruit-packing barn is now the tasting room. The winery is named after Dick’s grandfather, Lafayette. The first vintage followed in 1986. In 2013 the Renos sold to Gene Pierce and Scott Welliver, owners of neighbouring Glenora and Knapp, who run it as a separate estate.

The Renos pulled out the old Catawba, Niagara and Concord vines and replanted some 50 acres with vinifera, mostly Riesling and Chardonnay but also Bordeaux varieties, among them Cabernet Sauvignon. The winery’s Rieslings have won New York’s Governor’s Cup three times. This 2023 Cabernet Sauvignon is an estate wine, aged for 11 months in a mix of French and American oak and bottled at a moderate 12.5% alcohol.

The winery describes blackberries and toasted oak on the nose, with blackberry, graphite and violet on the palate, medium-plus tannins and a finish of red cherry and a little chocolate. It should keep improving for several years. Drunk now, the winery suggests sirloin, leaner cuts, braised meats and roast beef. The 2023 won a gold medal and 92 points at the 2025 New York State Wine Classic.
